title: Tate McRae releases "Housewife" with a lavish new video
excerpt: Tate McRae released "Housewife" on October 15, pairing a new single about money and independence with a lavish music video filmed in the south of France.
body:
Tate McRae released "Housewife" on October 15, pairing a new single about money and independence with a lavish music video filmed in the south of France. Issued through RCA Records, the song follows her 2025 album *So Close to What* and its subsequent touring run. The title suggests a familiar domestic role, yet here it describes a woman with enough money and freedom to set the terms of her own life.

The announcement artwork carried the joke before the song was released. In the image announcing "Housewife," McRae posed in a red bikini next to a baby stroller overflowing with cash. The setting was an extravagant villa rather than a family home. It was a striking introduction to the song's premise, replacing the conventional symbols of domestic responsibility with the money to avoid answering to anyone else. The stroller helped establish the humor even before the lyrics made it explicit.

At the center of the chorus is a wish to "be my own housewife." She wants wealth and a relationship, but not financial dependence on a partner. Romance is something she can choose, not something she needs to secure her future. The references to fame complicate that confidence, because the success that buys freedom can also impose its own demands. That contrast gives a playful title room for something more personal than another celebration of expensive possessions.

The official video carries the fantasy into a different setting. Directed by photographer Pierre-Ange Carlotti, it was shot in the south of France and moves between a sprawling estate, gardens and a yacht. Choreography by Sergio Reis places McRae's dancing inside the polished world of the film. The locations are beautiful enough to resemble a luxury advertisement, but the relationship at the center of the story gradually becomes more complicated.

[youtube:DPEodkHzH-s]

The video does not leave its protagonist entirely satisfied with having everything. As the romance grows strained, the glamorous surroundings become less reassuring. Its closing scene finds McRae tossing a coin into a wishing well and smiling, a small gesture after so much conspicuous wealth. The image allows the film to end with something it cannot buy: the hope that a private wish might come true.

Speaking at the launch of her TATE 01 fragrance on October 16, McRae described "Housewife" as a song with several meanings. She discussed the freedom to adopt different roles rather than accept the ones projected onto her by relationships or the music industry. In her telling, being feminine and being in control are not competing ambitions. The character in the video can enjoy the glamorous lifestyle without allowing it to decide who she must be.

Since the release of *So Close to What*, her concerts have grown more elaborate, from the Miss Possessive tour to major summer festival sets. Those productions foreground her ability to carry an elaborate spectacle through choreography. "Housewife" brings the same attention to presentation into a tightly focused story, using one relationship to put its central boast under pressure. The fantasy is deliberately excessive, but the uncomfortable question beneath it is familiar: can independence and intimacy coexist without either becoming a compromise?

Three days after the single's release, she brought "Housewife" to the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles on October 18. Dressed in a red corset and carrying a matching microphone, she performed it during the runway show alongside "Sports Car" and "Dear God." The appearance turned the new song into a live number almost immediately, with the singer's movement and staging doing the work previously handled by the villa, the yacht and the camera.
